newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The government has made a number of changes to its draft bill on tax legislation - now being discussed at the parliamentary committee level - indicating its willingness to back down in the face of some protests.
--A new wave of strikes, meanwhile, is expected to hit the country as of Monday. These will include seamen, teachers and possibly civil servants.

--The National Bank will adopt an overtly aggressive business policy this year, with mergers of insurance companies belonging to the Group, a major share capital increase with offers in Greece and abroad and expansion of its international activity on stock exchanges. The country's biggest bank will also play an active role in the bolstering of competition in the banking system.
--Increased competition between middle and larger-size retailers will mean curtains for small businesses.

--Interest will be centred on Prime Minister Costas Simitis's address to the fledgling National Agricultural Policy Council, to convene for the first time tomorrow. Close associates say there will be no dramatic announcements, but a restatement of pre-election pledges.
--Smiles at the Athens bourse yesterday as the general price index broke the thousand-point barrier for the first time in 10 months to close at 1,002.30, up 1.24 percent.

--The National Bank has plans to internationalise the drachma with 24-hour dealing rooms around the world. The first step will be to open the bank's Athens dealing room from 7 a.m. as of February 3 nad keep the London dealing room open until 8 p.m.
--The tax on derivatives is in force as of yesterday, following the tabling of an amendment to legislation in parliament by Deputy Finance Minister George Drys.
--Tax breaks on group insurance plans taken out by employers for staff will be partially maintained, under the amendments submitted by Drys.

--The report by auditors on the 65 Athens Stock Exchange members is now in the hands of the special prosecutor and the Capital Market Commission, who will both impose pecuniary measures where necessary.
--The Greek informatics market has seen a significant fall in profits in the last three years.
--The new economic crimes squad will have special powers in accordance with a new presidential decree, allowing it access to confidential papers in the banking, stock exchange and business sectors.
--CPI inflation fell to 7.5 percent yr/yr in December, falling but not necessarily "converging". NAFTEMBORIKI
--1997 inflation figures will be calculated with a new consumer index. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
